examples.ko: 친구 모임에서 신입생이 개인기를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: At the gathering, the freshman showed off a party trick.
My younger brother's special talent is doing impressions.
This player's individual skill is outstanding.

examples.ko: 개인기를 보여 달라고 해서 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: They asked for a party trick, so I sang a song.
In team games, teamwork matters more than individual skill.
I had no party trick, so I just laughed.

explain: 쓰임이 두 가지예요. 축구나 농구에서는 드리블 같은 선수 한 사람의 기술이고, 모임에서는 성대모사나 춤처럼 보여 주는 재주예요. '개인기를 보여 주다', '개인기가 좋다'처럼 써요. 팀워크와 반대로 말할 때도 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 개인기가 좋아서 인기가 많아요.
phrases.en: That player has great individual skill, so he is popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람의 기술이나 재주가 뛰어나다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise someone's outstanding personal skill or talent.

phrases.en: I prepared a party trick for the welcome party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에서 보여 줄 재주를 미리 생각해 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when preparing a talent to show at a gathering.

phrases.en: My friends took turns showing off their tricks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 사람이 차례로 재주를 보여 주는 분위기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people taking turns showing off their talents.

explain_en: It has two uses. In sports like soccer or basketball it means one player's skill, such as dribbling. At a gathering it means a trick, like an impression or a dance. It is also set against teamwork.

examples.en: That player signed with a new club.
The club plans to build a new stadium.

examples.ko: 우리 구단은 팬들에게 작은 선물을 줬어요.
examples.en: Our club gave the fans a small gift.

examples.ko: 이 구단에서 십 년 동안 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I played for this club for ten years.
The club's new manager was announced today.
A problem came up between the player and the club.

explain: '팀'은 선수들이 모인 팀이고, 구단은 그 팀을 운영하는 조직과 회사까지 포함해요. 선수가 '구단과 계약하다', '구단에서 뛰다'처럼 말해요. 친구끼리 응원하는 팀을 말할 때는 보통 '팀'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 이 구단에서 십 년 동안 뛰었어요.
phrases.en: That player played for this club for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수가 어느 팀 소속으로 경기한다는 뜻이에요. '구단'은 팀을 운영하는 조직까지 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a player plays for a certain team. '구단' also refers to the organization that runs the team.

phrases.en: The club staff help the players.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수가 아니라 구단에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for people who work for the club rather than the players.

phrases.en: The club owner came to the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구단을 가지고 있는 사람이나 회사의 대표를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who owns the club, or the head of the company that owns it.

explain_en: A '팀' is the group of players, while 구단 also includes the organization or company that runs it. Players '구단과 계약하다' or '구단에서 뛰다'. Fans chatting about the team they support usually just say '팀'.

examples.en: A school anniversary ceremony was held at the school.
The president also attended the ceremony.
The ceremony took about an hour.
We were busy preparing for the ceremony.
After the ceremony, everyone took photos.
The ceremony was cancelled too because of the rain.

explain: '-식'은 행사를 뜻해서 졸업식, 입학식, 결혼식처럼 여러 말에 붙어요. 기념식은 '열리다', '참석하다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: A commemoration ceremony will be held at school tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 시작되고 진행될 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for when the event takes place.

phrases.en: I attended the ceremony with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에 직접 가서 함께할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you go to and take part in the event.

phrases.en: The company held a tenth-anniversary ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 하는 쪽이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the organizer is the subject.

explain_en: The ending -식 means a ceremony, as in 졸업식, 입학식, and 결혼식. 기념식 is used with verbs like 열리다 and 참석하다.

examples.en: I went to my nephew's first birthday party.
At the first birthday party, the baby picked up the money.
These days people hold a small first birthday party with just family.
I prepared a gold ring as a gift for the first birthday party.

examples.ko: 돌잔치 사진을 보니 아기가 너무 귀여웠어요.
examples.en: The baby looked so cute in the first birthday party photos.

examples.ko: 내일 돌잔치가 있어서 한복을 입고 갈 거예요.
examples.en: There's a first birthday party tomorrow, so I'll wear hanbok.

explain: 아기가 태어나서 한 살이 되는 날 하는 잔치예요. 이날 '돌잡이'라고 해서 아기 앞에 실, 돈, 연필 등을 놓고 무엇을 집는지 보는 풍습이 있어요. 한 살 생일 자체는 '돌'이라고 하고, 그 뒤부터는 '생일'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: We're having our baby's first birthday party next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기의 첫 생일 잔치를 연다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to say you hold a first birthday party.
phrases.en_equiv: to hold a first birthday party

phrases.en: At the doljabi, the baby picked up a pencil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌잔치에서 아기가 무엇을 집는지 보는 풍습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The custom at a doljanchi of seeing what the baby picks up.

phrases.en: I invited my friend to my nephew's first birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잔치에 사람을 부를 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for inviting people to the party.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite to a first birthday party

explain_en: 돌잔치 is the party held when a baby turns one. A custom called 돌잡이 puts items like thread, money and a pencil in front of the baby to see which one is picked. The first birthday itself is 돌; later birthdays are 생일.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 마지막 주자에게 바통을 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Our class passed the baton to the last runner.
We dropped the baton, so our team lost.

examples.ko: 바통 터치가 아주 부드러워서 기록이 좋았어요.
examples.en: The baton pass was very smooth, so our time was good.

examples.ko: 선배에게서 바통을 이어받아 새 책임자가 됐어요.
examples.en: I took over from my senior and became the new person in charge.
The baton slipped out of my hand in the relay.
If you run without a baton, it isn't a relay.

explain: 계주에서 쓰는 막대지만 일을 넘겨주고 받는 이야기에도 많이 써요. '바통 터치'는 말 그대로 넘겨주는 동작이면서 '업무 인수인계'의 뜻으로도 말해요.

phrases.example: 이번 달부터 제가 팀장 일의 바통을 이어받았어요.
phrases.en: From this month, I took over the team leader's work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞사람이 하던 일이나 책임을 이어서 맡을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when you take over work or responsibility that someone before you was handling.
phrases.en_equiv: to take over the baton; to pick up the torch

explain_en: It is the stick used in relay races, but people also use it when talking about handing work over to someone. '바통 터치' is the actual handoff and is also used for handing over duties.

examples.en: We played a treasure hunt on the picnic and got a gift.
The kids joined the treasure hunt in the park with excitement.

examples.ko: 보물찾기 쪽지는 나무 뒤에 숨겨져 있었어요.
examples.en: The treasure hunt slip was hidden behind a tree.

examples.ko: 저는 보물찾기를 한 번도 이겨 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never once won a treasure hunt.

examples.ko: 보물찾기는 찾는 재미가 있어서 어른도 좋아해요.
examples.en: Treasure hunts are fun to search for, so adults like them too.

examples.ko: 생일 파티 때 집 안에서 보물찾기를 준비했어요.
examples.en: For the birthday party, I prepared a treasure hunt inside the house.

explain: '보물찾기'는 한국 학교의 소풍 때 꼭 하는 놀이로 유명해요. 선생님이 쪽지를 숨기고 아이들이 찾아서 선물과 바꾸는 방식이에요. 발음은 [보물찯끼]로 나고, '보물 찾기'라고 띄어 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The children played a treasure hunt game in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀이'를 붙이면 아이들이 하는 게임이라는 느낌이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 놀이 makes it clearer that it's a game for kids.

phrases.en: We had a treasure hunt at the birthday party.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic usage, with 하다.

phrases.en: The teacher hid the treasure in the grass.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보물찾기를 준비하는 사람이 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes what the person setting up the hunt does.

explain_en: 보물찾기 is famous in Korea as a game almost always played on school picnics. The teacher hides slips of paper, and kids find them and exchange them for prizes. It is pronounced [보물찯끼] and written as one word.

examples.ko: 산 입구에 오래된 비석이 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old stone monument stands at the mountain entrance.
A name is carved on the stone.
I laid flowers and paid my respects in front of the gravestone.

examples.ko: 이 마을에는 옛 장군의 비석이 있어요.
examples.en: This village has a stone monument for an old general.
The writing on the stone is worn and hard to read.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 비석에 학교의 역사가 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The school's history is written on the monument in front of it.

explain: 무덤 앞의 돌은 '묘비', 사건이나 사람을 기념해 세운 돌은 '기념비'예요. '비석'은 이런 돌을 두루 가리키고 관광지 앞에서 자주 보여요. '표지석'은 장소를 알려 주는 돌이에요.

phrases.en: They put up a stone monument at the village entrance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기념하려고 비석을 만들어 둘 때 '세우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 세우다 is used when putting up a monument.

phrases.en: I took a photo in front of the stone monument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관광지에서 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to point out a spot at tourist places.

phrases.en: There is a memorial stone in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건이나 사람을 기념하는 돌을 더 정확하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more exact word for a stone that honors an event or person.

explain_en: A stone at a grave is a '묘비', and one set up to commemorate an event or person is a '기념비'. '비석' broadly covers these stones and is often seen at tourist spots. A '표지석' is a stone that marks a place.

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 수호신을 모신 나무가 있어요.
examples.en: At the village entrance is a tree that enshrines the guardian spirit.

examples.ko: 이 부적은 나를 지켜 주는 수호신 같아요.
examples.en: This charm feels like a guardian that protects me.
In that game I became the guardian.
Grandma said the jangseung is the village's guardian spirit.
Our team's guardian angel is the goalkeeper.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 이 곰 인형이 제 수호신이었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, this teddy bear was my protector.

explain: 원래는 마을이나 집을 지켜 준다고 믿는 신이지만, 지금은 비유로 더 자주 써요. 중요한 순간마다 나를 지켜 주는 사람이나 물건을 '수호신'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: This tree is regarded as the village's guardian deity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 뜻대로 마을을 지켜 주는 신을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the original sense of a deity protecting a village.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 저에게 수호신 같은 친구예요.
phrases.en: That friend is like a guardian spirit to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들 때 늘 도와주는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A metaphor for someone who always helps in hard times.
phrases.en_equiv: a friend like a guardian spirit

phrases.example: 이 인형이 시험 날 수호신이 되어 줬어요.
phrases.en: This doll became my guardian on exam day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 물건이나 사람이 나를 지켜 주는 존재가 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an object or person becomes a protector for you.

explain_en: Originally a god believed to protect a village or home, but today it is more often used figuratively. A person or object that protects you at key moments is called a 수호신.

examples.en: My favorite author released a new work.
A new movie opens this week.
This new work was as fun as I hoped.
I bought a newly released novel at the bookstore.
The reaction to the new work is very good.
The director chose the lead of the new work himself.

explain: 책·영화·음악·게임처럼 새로 나온 작품에 써요. 옷이나 제품은 '신상품', '신제품'이라고 해요. 앞서 낸 작품은 '전작'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I bought a new novel at the bookstore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 나온 책 중 소설을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a newly released novel.

phrases.example: 그 가수가 다음 달에 신작을 내요.
phrases.en: That singer will release a new work next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작가나 가수가 새 작품을 내놓는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an artist releasing a new work.

phrases.example: 신작 게임이 나와서 친구와 같이 했어요.
phrases.en: A new game came out, so I played it with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 출시된 게임에도 '신작'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '신작' is also used for newly released games.

explain_en: Use it for newly released works such as books, films, music, and games. Clothes or products are '신상품' or '신제품'. A previous work by the same creator is '전작'.

examples.ko: 그 선수가 오늘 안타를 세 개 쳤어요.
examples.en: That player got three hits today.
A hit came in the ninth inning and we scored.

examples.ko: 안타 하나만 치면 이길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we get just one hit, we can win.
Sadly, we got no hits at all.
That batter gets hits well.

examples.ko: 두 번 연속 안타를 치고 나갔어요.
examples.en: He got on base with two hits in a row.

explain: 야구에서 타자가 공을 쳐서 아웃되지 않고 베이스까지 나가는 일이에요. '안타를 치다', '안타가 나오다'라고 해요. 한 선수가 안타를 세 개 치면 '3안타'처럼 숫자를 앞에 붙여요. 소리가 비슷한 '안타깝다'와는 관계가 없어요.

phrases.example: 우리 팀 선수가 첫 타석에서 안타를 쳤어요.
phrases.en: Our player got a hit in his first at-bat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타자가 안타를 만들 때 쓰는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for a batter getting a hit.

phrases.en: That player had three hits yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자를 앞에 붙여 한 경기의 안타 수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A number goes in front to give the hit count for a game.

phrases.en: The pitcher gave up two hits.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투수 입장에서 안타를 허용했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the pitcher's side when allowing a hit.

explain_en: In baseball, a batter hits the ball and reaches base without being put out. You say '안타를 치다' or '안타가 나오다'. A player with three hits is described as '3안타', with the number in front. The similar-sounding '안타깝다' (to feel sorry) is unrelated.

examples.en: That pitcher is our team's ace.
The sales team's ace received an award.
The coach entrusted the last game to the ace.
The star player scored at the end.
I played the ace in the card game.
The star of our class is a runner.

explain: 운동 팀뿐 아니라 직장이나 학교에서 가장 믿음직하고 뛰어난 사람에게도 써요. 카드 게임의 A 카드도 '에이스'라고 해요.

phrases.en: That player is the ace of our team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀에서 가장 믿음직한 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the most dependable person on a team.

phrases.en: The ace player got hurt, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선수'를 붙여 운동 팀의 가장 뛰어난 선수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 선수 points to the best player on a sports team.

phrases.example: 그는 입사 삼 년 만에 회사의 에이스가 됐어요.
phrases.en: He became the company's ace after three years at the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실력이 가장 뛰어난 사람이 되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say someone became the top performer.

explain_en: It is used not only for sports teams but also for the most dependable and outstanding person at a workplace or school. The A card in card games is also called 에이스.

examples.en: My mother does gardening as a hobby.

examples.ko: 원예 용품은 꽃집이나 마트에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy gardening supplies at a flower shop or a supermarket.
I got interested in gardening and bought a flower pot.

examples.ko: 원예가 취미인 분이 많아서 주말 농장이 인기예요.
examples.en: Many people enjoy gardening, so weekend farms are popular.

examples.ko: 베란다에서 하는 원예는 작은 공간에서도 가능해요.
examples.en: Gardening on a balcony is possible even in a small space.
This university has a horticulture department.

explain: '농사'보다 꽃·채소·화분을 가꾸는 취미의 느낌이 강해요. '원예 용품', '원예 치료'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여 많이 써요. 집 마당이나 베란다에서 식물을 키우는 이야기에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The hospital held a horticultural therapy class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물을 키우면서 마음을 편하게 하는 활동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to calming the mind by growing plants.

phrases.en: Gardening is my hobby these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물 가꾸기를 취미로 말할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Natural for describing plant care as a hobby.

phrases.en: I learn gardening at the culture center every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이나 화분 가꾸는 방법을 공부할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying how to care for flowers and pots.

explain_en: Compared with '농사' (farming), it has a stronger feeling of a hobby of tending flowers, vegetables and potted plants. It often comes before another noun, as in '원예 용품' and '원예 치료'. It suits talk about growing plants in a yard or on a balcony.

en: to rest; to get away; to relax

examples.ko: 의사가 한 달 동안 시골에서 휴양하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to rest in the countryside for a month.
He read books while relaxing at the beach.
My hobby is getting away to the mountains every weekend.
I rested at home until my body recovered.
The hotel is full of people who came to relax.
This summer I'm going to relax on Jeju Island.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '쉬다', '푹 쉬다'가 훨씬 흔해요. '휴양하다'는 병이나 피로를 회복하려고 쉴 때, 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. '휴양지에서 휴양하다'는 말이 겹치니 '휴양지에서 쉬다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I rested well at home on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '휴양하다'보다 이 말이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk this is much more natural than 휴양하다.

phrases.en: Grandmother went to the seaside to recuperate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬는 것이 목적인 여행을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a trip whose purpose is rest.

phrases.example: 아버지는 병 때문에 시골에서 휴양하고 있어요.
phrases.en: My father is recuperating in the countryside because of an illness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 피로를 풀려고 쉬는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means resting to recover from illness or fatigue.

explain_en: In daily talk '쉬다' or '푹 쉬다' is much more common. '휴양하다' shows up more in writing and news, for resting to recover from illness or fatigue. '휴양지에서 휴양하다' repeats itself, so '휴양지에서 쉬다' sounds more natural.
